newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen falling on Brazil tumble.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen falling on Brazil tumble.

text.p: Hurt by a steady selloff on the Brazilian markets, Argentine stocks were expected to stretch Monday's losses at the opening Tuesday, dealers said.
"The bolsa will continue the correction it began late yesterday when it was hit by devaluation fears in Brazil," said Leonardo Torres Barsati at analysts Rio Research.

The weighted MerVal index fell 1.7 percent Monday to 836.14, its heaviest drop since April, on talk Brazil might follow in the footsteps of Southeast Asian nations and face a big devaluation. Brazil's Bovespa index was off 4.8 percent midsession Tuesday after losing 3.5 percent Monday.
"The Brazilian factor is the excuse the bolsa here needed to take profits -- everybody knew we were heading for a near-term correction but we needed some bad news to latch onto," Barsanti said.
Dealers noted volume shrank Monday as prices fell and predicted if prices shed another 2.0 percent, many players would be lured back into the market.
"This can be the buying opportunity many investors wanted, so although profit-taking may last several days, after the initial hit I don't think we will see very sharp losses," another dealer said.
Investors will track market bellwether oil giant YPF after a judge blocked the planned flotation Tuesday of 10 percent of company shares awarded to workers.
YPF said the deal was put off "briefly" and it was seeking to resolve the challenge presented by a small group of employees who left the firm before it was privatized in 1993.
When the secondary offering is finally carried out the stock will fetch a price of around $30, dealers estimated.

"A really good price would be $33," Barsanti said. "But demand won't be massive because the market has gone up so much recently. Otherwise, it's a good buy compared to other leading international oil companies."
